generated_by: research/nfl lessons; each row cites the artifact or official page that produced it

lessons.finding: A transparent efficiency rating (points for/against, opponent-adjusted, home field, season decay) does NOT beat the closing spread.
lessons.evidence: 2025 holdout: 172 spread bets, ROI -1.2% (CI -12.3% to +10.4%); 2024 check: 189 bets, -8.1%.
lessons.implication: Signal design must add information the closing line already lacks, not re-derive team strength.

lessons.finding: Totals are harder than spreads with this model.
lessons.implication: Totals need a different feature set (pace, weather, pace-of-play, red-zone), not a margin model.

lessons.finding: Betting underdogs on a model edge loses at this calibration level.
lessons.evidence: 2025: 219 moneyline dogs, ROI -7.5%, win rate 30.1%; 2024: -20.2% with a CI that excludes zero on the downside.
lessons.implication: Probability edges in the tail (dogs) need much larger samples and better calibration than a normal-approximation model provides.

lessons.finding: Spread cover and total over are close to independent in the historical sample.
lessons.evidence: 2,792 games: phi +0.022 (clustered CI -0.010..+0.056), joint 24.39% vs 23.83% independent (ratio 1.023).
lessons.implication: For this pair, an independence price is defensible, but the ratio must be shown and re-tested each season.

lessons.finding: Cross-game legs show apparent dependence of +0.099 that is not significant at n=234.
lessons.implication: This is what noise looks like at parlay sample sizes; any 'parlay edge' below ~0.1 correlation is invisible without thousands of pairs.

lessons.finding: Only 6 of 275 Week 10 injury rows carry an explicit game status on the day read.
lessons.implication: Practice participation is not a status. Any injury model must carry a 'status not yet set' state, or it will overstate certainty.

lessons.finding: Depth deficiency is computable for any club that publishes a depth chart, and the clubs do publish them on their own domains.
lessons.evidence: WAS/NYG/DET charts read; 13 starter-level deficiencies derived; e.g. WAS CB Amik Robertson limited -> Mike Sainristil (string 2).
lessons.implication: League-wide tracking is a capture problem, not a data-permission problem.

lessons.finding: Community game logs can lag the official pages by a day (three 2026 rows missing).
lessons.evidence: AZ season totals, AZ@SEA (W9), LA@AZ (W10) missing from the file on 2026-11-12 while NFL.com shows them.
lessons.implication: Never let a community file drive a published official claim; reconcile first, publish second.

lessons.finding: One of the two community sources has no license file.
lessons.evidence: GitHub metadata: leesharpe/nfldata license = null (2026-11-12); nflverse-data is CC-BY-4.0.
lessons.implication: A backtest built on unlicensed data cannot support a public profitability claim.

lessons.finding: A model that is 60% right on margin sign still loses money after vig.
lessons.evidence: 2025 model sign accuracy 59.9% vs the market's 85.3% (market covers when it agrees with the result).
lessons.implication: Directional accuracy is a vanity metric; only post-vig ROI with a lower bound matters.

lessons.finding: Five of the eight frozen candidates cannot be tested at all with the data the project holds.
lessons.evidence: S4 (no opening lines), S5 (no props), S6/S7 (no prop outcomes/prices), S8 (no injury archive).
lessons.implication: Most of the 'combo/parlay strategy' space is data-blocked, not model-blocked.

lessons.finding: The 2025 holdout throws away three of the five signals as soon as the price assumption is honest.
lessons.evidence: -110 is assumed for historical bets; real prices vary from -105 to -115.
lessons.implication: A 1-2 cent price error is the same order as the entire edge being hunted.
